prompts.name: search
prompts.description: Arbor-compatible search source over Confluence: runs one CQL query and returns ranked, cited results in arbor's normalized SearchResultSet/RankedResult envelope (lightweight retrieval, no download/summarize). Designed to be registered as a federated source in arbor's .kbs/.arbor.json and to degrade gracefully (soft error, never throws) when the Atlassian MCP is unavailable.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: The search text

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of results to return

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Content-type filter; honored when 'page' or 'blogpost', otherwise ignored

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description: Source-specific filters: { spaces: [space keys], dateRange: CQL date clause }

parameters.name: timeoutMs
parameters.description: Soft time budget; return available results with partial=true if exceeded

returns.description: A SearchResultSet in arbor's Search Source contract shape. Never throws; soft failures are reported via error + partial.

partial.description: True when results were truncated or the source was skipped due to a soft error

error.description: Soft error when the source could not run, else null

results.description: Ranked results (RankedResult shape). Empty means no matches — not an error.

score.description: Source-relative rank score; not comparable across sources

prompts.name: createStory
prompts.description: Create a new Jira Story with required project fields, optional acceptance criteria in ADF format, and proper field validation

parameters.name: projectKey
parameters.description: Jira project key the story should be created in (e.g., 'AIP', 'PCG'). When omitted, the workflow falls back to top-level defaultProjectKey in .ai/jira.config.json. If neither is set, the workflow halts with DefaultProjectKeyMissingError.

parameters.name: summary
parameters.description: Story title / summary

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: Story description in markdown format

parameters.name: acceptanceCriteria
parameters.description: Acceptance criteria as a comma-separated or newline-separated list

parameters.name: labels
parameters.description: Comma-separated labels to apply to the story

parameters.name: parentKey
parameters.description: Issue key of the parent Epic to link this story under (the Epic Link / parent relationship), e.g., 'PROJ-100'. When omitted, the story is created without a parent.

parameters.name: storyPoints
parameters.description: Numeric story-point estimate written to the configured Story Points field as a bare number. Setting it at create time avoids a follow-up edit in projects whose workflow requires points before a story may leave Backlog.

throws.title: ConfigInvalidError
throws.description: The .ai/jira.config.json file exists but failed schema validation. The workflow halts before attempting to create or update an issue. Run the verify-jira-config skill to see violations.

configPath.description: Absolute path to the offending config file

throws.title: BootstrapFailedError
throws.description: The configure-jira skill reported success but the freshly-written .ai/jira.config.json could not be loaded or validated on the follow-up load-jira-config call. Indicates an unexpected discrepancy between write and read.

configPath.description: Absolute path the configure-jira skill reported writing

details.description: Why the post-write load failed (parse error, schema violation, missing file)

throws.title: ProjectNotInConfigError
throws.description: The .ai/jira.config.json file exists and is valid, but has no entry under config.projects for the requested project key. The workflow halts and the calling agent should offer to bootstrap the missing project via the configure-jira skill with projectKey=<requested>.

requestedProjectKey.description: The project key the workflow attempted to resolve

availableProjectKeys.description: Project keys currently configured in the file

configPath.description: Absolute path to the loaded config file

throws.title: DefaultProjectKeyMissingError
throws.description: The .ai/jira.config.json file is valid but the workflow could not resolve a project key — the calling prompt did not supply a projectKey parameter and config.defaultProjectKey is unset. The workflow halts; the user must either supply projectKey explicitly or run the configure-jira skill to set defaultProjectKey.

availableProjectKeys.description: Project keys configured in the file (the user can pick one to pass as projectKey)

configPath.description: Absolute path to the loaded config file

prompts.name: createEpic
prompts.description: Create a new Jira Epic via the create-jira-issues workflow skill. Uses the Epic profile (acceptanceCriteriaMode = inline-description by default since most projects, including AIP, do not expose the AC custom field on Epic; flips to adf-field when the project does expose it). Supports the standard priority field and optional Epic-specific custom fields (Epic Name, target start/end dates, theme).

parameters.name: projectKey
parameters.description: Jira project key the epic should be created in (e.g., 'AIP', 'PCG'). When omitted, the workflow falls back to top-level defaultProjectKey in .ai/jira.config.json. If neither is set, the workflow halts with DefaultProjectKeyMissingError.

parameters.name: summary
parameters.description: Epic title / summary (also serves as the Epic Name in modern Jira)

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: Epic description in markdown format

parameters.name: acceptanceCriteria
parameters.description: Acceptance criteria as a comma-separated or newline-separated list. Default mode appends them as a `## Acceptance Criteria` section in the description (inline-description); when the project exposes the AC custom field on Epic, the workflow sets it via a separate ADF API call instead.

parameters.name: labels
parameters.description: Comma-separated labels to apply

parameters.name: priority
parameters.description: Priority name as defined in the target Jira instance (e.g. 'High', 'Medium', 'Low', or 'Highest'/'Lowest' where the project defines them). Sent as the standard priority field in object form: {"name": "<priority>"}. Omit to let the project default apply. Names are instance-specific and passed through unchanged; an unknown name returns FIELD_VALIDATION_FAILED.

parameters.name: epicName
parameters.description: Separate Epic Name field, when the consuming Jira project keeps Epic Name distinct from summary

parameters.name: targetStartDate
parameters.description: Target start date in YYYY-MM-DD format

parameters.name: targetEndDate
parameters.description: Target end date in YYYY-MM-DD format

parameters.name: theme
parameters.description: Epic theme value, when the consuming project defines themes

Supports summary, description, acceptance criteria, labels, priority, status transition, assignee, and optional Epic-specific custom fields (Epic Name, target start/end dates, theme).

parameters.name: acceptanceCriteria

parameters.name: acMergeMode

parameters.name: priority
parameters.description: Updated priority name as defined in the target Jira instance (e.g. 'High', 'Medium', 'Low'). Sent as the standard priority field in object form: {"name": "<priority>"}. Omit to leave the current priority untouched; there is no clear token, since Jira issues always carry a priority.

prompts.name: configureJira
prompts.description: Generate or update one project entry in .ai/jira.config.json by discovering the team's live Jira project field configuration via MCP and capturing per-team defaults. Multi-project safe: when an existing config has entries for other projects, this prompt merges the new entry into config.projects rather than overwriting the file. Run once per Jira project the team works in.

parameters.name: projectKey
parameters.description: Jira project key to configure against (e.g., 'AIP'). When omitted, the prompt asks the user.

parameters.name: siteUrl
parameters.description: Atlassian site URL (e.g., https://pennymac.atlassian.net). When omitted, the prompt detects via validate-mcp-connection.

parameters.name: force
parameters.description: Skip the per-project replace-confirmation prompt when an entry already exists for projectKey. Does not suppress the final write-permission prompt. Default: false.

returns.description: Result of the configuration generation or update for one project entry

configPath.description: Absolute path to the written .ai/jira.config.json file

projectKey.description: Project key whose entry was added or replaced

replaceMode.description: How the file was modified: add (new project added to existing file), replace (existing entry overwritten), create-file (no file existed; new file created)

projectsAfterWrite.description: Project keys present in the file after the merge — useful for the calling workflow to confirm no previously-configured projects were dropped

fieldsResolved.description: Count of logical field IDs resolved to a customfield_NNN value for this project

fieldsUnresolved.description: Count of logical field IDs left as null because the project does not expose them

defaultsConfigured.description: Count of per-team defaults the user supplied for this project

issueTypesProfiled.description: Names of issue types whose field metadata was inspected

driftReport.description: Result of the post-write verify-jira-config sanity check (single-project mode against the freshly-written project)

throws.title: ConfigInvalidError
throws.description: An existing .ai/jira.config.json was found but failed schema validation. The configure-jira skill halts to avoid merging a new project entry into a malformed file. The user must hand-fix or replace the file before re-running.

prompts.name: verifyJiraConfig
prompts.description: Detect drift between the team's .ai/jira.config.json and live Jira project(s). Multi-project: when projectKey is supplied, verifies that single project; when omitted, iterates every entry in config.projects and returns a multi-project envelope with one DriftReport per project. Compares configured field IDs, AC handling modes, and required-field coverage against MCP discovery data. Read-only — never mutates Jira state.

parameters.name: projectKey
parameters.description: Jira project key to verify against. When provided, runs in single-project mode. When omitted, runs in all-projects mode and iterates every entry in config.projects.

parameters.name: issueTypes
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of issue type names to verify (e.g., 'Story,Epic'). Defaults to all issue types each project exposes. Applied uniformly to every project in all-projects mode.

returns.description: Drift detection report. Shape varies by mode: single-project returns a flat report; all-projects returns an envelope containing per-project sub-reports under projects.<KEY>.

outcome.description: Aggregated outcome. In single-project mode this is the project's outcome. In all-projects mode: no-drift if all projects pass; drift-detected if any project has drift; partial-failure if at least one project errored AND another succeeded; total-failure if every project errored.

mode.description: Which verification mode produced this report

projectKey.description: Present only in single-project mode — the project that was verified

findings.description: Drift findings grouped by category. Present only when outcome = drift-detected in single-project mode.

projects.description: Present only in all-projects mode — map of project key to per-project sub-report. Each value has the shape { outcome, projectKey, issueTypesChecked?, findings? } matching a single-project report (minus mode and configPath).

throws.title: NoConfigError
throws.description: No .ai/jira.config.json exists at any of the searched paths.

throws.title: ProjectNotInConfigError
throws.description: Single-project mode only: the supplied projectKey has no entry under config.projects.

throws.title: EmptyProjectsConfigError
throws.description: All-projects mode only: config.projects exists but is empty (no projects to verify). Run the configure-jira skill to add at least one project.

throws.title: ProjectNotAccessibleError
throws.description: Single-project mode only: the Jira project is unreachable or the user lacks access. In all-projects mode this is captured per-project inside projects.<KEY>.outcome instead.

prompts.name: linkIssues
prompts.description: Create directional links between existing Jira issues (Blocks, Relates, Duplicate, Clones) via the link-jira-issues workflow skill. Discovers the link types the instance actually defines, resolves direction (inwardIssue = blocker, outwardIssue = blocked), reads existing links so re-runs are idempotent, reports a reversed existing link as a conflict, and soft-skips when the requested type is unavailable. For dependency/blocking relationships only — the parent Epic relationship is the parentKey input on the create-jira-issues / update-jira-issues skills, not an issue link.

parameters.name: links
parameters.description: Links to create. Each entry is an object: { inwardIssue, outwardIssue, type?, comment? }. Pass an array of one to create a single link. For directional types, inwardIssue is the blocker and outwardIssue is the blocked issue — for a dependency edge where the dependent needs the predecessor, inwardIssue = predecessor and outwardIssue = dependent.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Default link type for entries that omit their own. Matched case-insensitively against the types the instance defines, including their inward/outward descriptions.

parameters.name: comment
parameters.description: Default comment for entries that omit one. Posted on the outward issue.

parameters.name: onTypeUnavailable
parameters.description: What to do when the instance does not define the requested link type. 'skip' returns success with every link reported as skipped, so a project-configuration gap does not block the caller's wider workflow; 'fail' raises LINK_TYPE_UNAVAILABLE.

parameters.name: dryRun
parameters.description: Resolve and report the planned links without creating any.

returns.description: Per-link outcome of the linking pass

success.description: True when the pass completed, including when every link was skipped. False only when nothing could be attempted.

resolvedType.description: The link type name as the instance defines it

skipped.description: Links not created, each with a reason (ALREADY_LINKED, TYPE_UNAVAILABLE)

conflicts.description: Pairs where a reverse link of the same type already exists; reported rather than overwritten

throws.title: ConnectionError
throws.description: The Atlassian MCP server is unreachable or unauthenticated

throws.title: LinkTypeUnavailableError
throws.description: The requested link type is not defined in this Jira instance and onTypeUnavailable = fail

throws.title: PermissionError
throws.description: The user lacks the Link Issues permission on the project

skills.name: validate-mcp-connection
skills.description: Validates the Atlassian MCP server connection by retrieving accessible resources and verifying user access. Use as a prerequisite before any Jira or Confluence operations.

skills.name: link-jira-issues
skills.description: Creates directional links between existing Jira issues (Blocks, Relates, Duplicate, Clones) via getIssueLinkTypes and createIssueLink. Discovers the link types the instance actually defines rather than assuming Blocks exists, resolves link direction (inwardIssue = blocker, outwardIssue = blocked), reads existing links first so re-runs do not duplicate, reports a reversed existing link as a conflict instead of overwriting it, and soft-skips when the requested type is unavailable. Covers issue links only — the parent Epic relationship is the parentKey input on the create-jira-issues / update-jira-issues skills.

skills.name: retrieve-jira
skills.description: Retrieves a specific Jira ticket by issue key and returns structured ticket data including summary, description, status, assignee, and priority.

skills.name: get-confluence-page
skills.description: Retrieves a specific Confluence page by page ID or title and returns the page content in markdown format with metadata.

skills.name: download-jiras
skills.description: Downloads multiple Jira tickets matching a JQL query or list of issue keys and saves each as a markdown file in a local directory.

skills.name: download-confluence-pages
skills.description: Downloads multiple Confluence pages and saves each as a markdown file in a local directory. Supports batch retrieval from search results or explicit page IDs.

skills.name: search-summarize-confluence
skills.description: Systematically searches Confluence for a topic using CQL queries, downloads all relevant content, analyzes and categorizes findings, and produces a comprehensive summary with key insights.

skills.name: search-jira
skills.description: Federated search entry point for the Atlassian source. Accepts arbor's SearchQuery envelope, runs a single CQL query over Confluence via the Atlassian MCP, and returns ranked, cited results in arbor's normalized SearchResultSet/RankedResult shape — lightweight retrieval (titles + excerpts), not a download/summarize pass. Never throws: connection, auth, and CQL failures come back as a soft error on the envelope so a federated search degrades gracefully. Executes the retrieval mechanics documented in confluence-search-source.

skills.name: confluence-search-source
skills.description: Arbor-compatible search source over Confluence. Runs a single CQL query via the Atlassian MCP and maps the top matches to ranked, cited results in arbor's SearchResultSet/RankedResult shape — lightweight retrieval (titles + excerpts), not a download/summarize workflow. Surfaces connection/auth problems as a soft error so a federated search degrades gracefully. Provides the retrieval mechanics the search-jira skill executes.

skills.name: create-jira-issues
skills.description: Drives the end-to-end create workflow for Jira stories, tasks, bugs, sub-tasks, and epics via the Atlassian MCP server. Loads an issue-type profile, assembles required + optional fields, asks user permission, creates the issue, dispatches acceptance-criteria handling (adf-field vs inline-description), and verifies the result.

skills.name: update-jira-issues
skills.description: Drives the end-to-end update workflow for existing Jira issues. Retrieves the current issue, builds a focused change set, asks user permission, applies updates across multiple editJiraIssue calls (markdown vs ADF separation), optionally transitions status, and verifies the result. Acceptance criteria support replace (default) or append/merge via acMergeMode.

skills.name: set-acceptance-criteria
skills.description: Sets the Acceptance Criteria field on an existing Jira issue using ADF JSON in a separate API call from any markdown updates. Supports acMergeMode: 'replace' (default, overwrites the whole AC field) or 'append' (merges new AC items into existing ones, deduped). Used by the create and update workflow skills, also callable directly when only AC needs to change.

skills.name: load-jira-config
skills.description: Locates and parses the per-team .ai/jira.config.json for the consuming repo, validates it against the package schema, and returns either a flat single-project view (resolved from the caller's projectKey input or defaultProjectKey) or the full multi-project config. Read-only filesystem skill — no MCP calls. Used by the create and update workflow skills (Step 2) and by verify-jira-config to resolve {{*FieldId}} placeholders deterministically against the right project's settings.

skills.name: configure-jira
skills.description: Generates or repairs one project entry in the consuming repo's .ai/jira.config.json by discovering that Jira project's live issue types and per-type field metadata via the Atlassian MCP, heuristically mapping the package's logical field names to the project's custom field IDs, capturing per-team default values, and writing the merged multi-project file behind an explicit user-approval gate. Multi-project safe — merges one project entry at a time and preserves every other entry. Invoked by the create and update workflow skills when the config is missing or has no entry for the active project.

skills.name: verify-jira-config
skills.description: Detects drift between .ai/jira.config.json and the live Jira project(s). Multi-project: verifies one project in single-project mode (when projectKey is supplied) or iterates every entry in config.projects in all-projects mode. Compares configured field IDs, AC handling modes, and required-field coverage against MCP discovery data. Emits a structured DriftReport. Read-only — invokes only getJiraProjectIssueTypesMetadata and getJiraIssueTypeMetaWithFields, never createJiraIssue/editJiraIssue.
